text:
james: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a small Feature Capability Descriptor (FCD) that runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private) return during control-plane handshake. Goal: let routing/policy make decisions without guessing features. Example payload idea:

```json
{
  "fcd_version": "1.0",
  "capabilities": ["kv_cache", "quantized_int8", "streaming", "function_calling"],
  "limits": {"max_seq": 4096, "concurrent_sessions": 32}
}
```

Questions: minimal fields? where to draw the trust line (no secrets in FCD, right?). How do we handle mismatched versions? thoughts on rollout strategy.

james: @anya tagging you for the policy side — can the router use FCD to pick fallbacks?

anya: I like it. Keep it tiny. version + capabilities list + optional limits. Router can pick fallback if capability missing, but need a clear policy: prefer semantic fallback (e.g., disable streaming -> use short-polling) not heuristic.

mike: +1 on tiny. Also: consider encoding as protobuf or CBOR for perf but keep JSON for readability. We should avoid any fields that imply secrets or customer identifiers. FCD = capabilities only.

sophia: Security note: Private deployments might expose internal-only capabilities (e.g., HSM-backed KMS flow). FCD should have a trust flag: "private_trusted": true/false? But careful — that leaks deployment class. Alternative: control-plane keeps the mapping and FCD returns stable capability tokens (opaque).

mike: opaque tokens complicate routing rules. If we have a short capability enum we can map those to allowed flows. Leaking hosting class might be ok inside our control plane, but not to customers. Keep internal vs external fields separate.

luis: For backwards compatibility: plan version negotiation: control-plane reads fcd_version, if unknown -> query for minimal probe (e.g., HEAD /runtime/capabilities?probe=true) and mark runtime as legacy. Add a 2-week canary starting with dedicated infra.

emma: Also consider automated regression rules: when a runtime claims a capability, run quick eval (5 sample prompts) to verify expected behavior (e.g., quantized_int8 quality threshold). If below threshold, mark capability degraded and add alert. Avoid silent quality regressions.

james: Good point emma. So action items: 1) define minimal FCD schema (v1: version, capabilities[], limits{}), 2) spec probe/legacy flow, 3) define fallback policy table (semantic fallback mapping), 4) add lightweight capability smoke-checks on registration. I'll draft an RFC with examples and a rollout plan starting in dedicated, then hosted, then private opt-in.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy starting: rtr-fcd-v1 -> infra-dedicated-us-west at 1748205710 :rocket:

anya: One more: include a TTL for FCD so we re-check periodically (e.g., 24h) — prevents stale capability claims after upgrades.

james: Agreed TTL. I'll include that. Thanks all — ping me if you want items assigned.
